scope: Official supported resolution path for Daily cross-account role access; no cloud mutation or repeated local-role audit.

current_evidence.advanced_activation: Parent reports management-account email verification has not been completed.
current_evidence.local_daily_role: Verified against current Daily requirements in live-daily-quick-role-review.json.

prerequisites: The Paid-plan prerequisite is already satisfied.
Owner completes management-account email verification in AWS Settings.
activation_steps: Settings → Projects → Actions → Explore advanced features
Choose the team name and management-account email
effects: Previously managed RCPs and SCPs become editable through management-account administration.
Project spend limits are removed; paused projects reactivate.
No promise that the external-principal deny is automatically removed.
policy_steps: Settings → Projects → Manage this organization → Manage policies
Use the management-account Organizations session, not the existing project role.
Read the exact applicable RCP, policy ID, ancestry and content hash.
If the observed deny matches the reviewed design, prepare its exact narrow Daily role exception against those actual bytes.
Retain unrelated restrictions and the existing Daily role trust/object scope.
supported_resolution.preserve: The AWS-managed organization-escape and managed-role protections are documented to remain after activation; they are not part of the Daily exception.
supported_resolution.verification: After an authorized exact policy correction, root runs the existing one-use verify_storage operator, requires cleanup-confirmed success, and checks a newly written exact test-object version before declaring storage acceptance.

classification_review.result: No concrete misclassification found. A generic invalid-request-error/HTTP400 alone cannot yield role_assumption_denied; the classifier also requires bounded provider-detail text identifying role assumption and failure/denial.
classification_review.uncertainty: Sanitized classification identifies a failed provider step, not the exact AWS policy.

references.supports: Activation prerequisites, owner email verification, administrative control, irreversible activation and spend-limit removal.
Explicit supported RCP editing path after activation.
Published external-principal deny and separate persistent baseline protections.
Daily trust requirements and root-level test upload verification.

next_actor: Root owns browser handoff, any policy read or mutation after activation, and provider acceptance.
